API mode on Pi: QA report

Mission #4070, phase 6 (section 7 of the mission document). Built 2026-10-20 04:44 UTC from 4 proof run(s): linux 20261020-010149, windows 20261020-015945, windows 20261020-021210, windows 20261020-041719.

Summary

linux, run 20261020-010149: every check passed (27 passed, 0 failed). Pi 1.2.0, commit 26a227479, tree clean.

windows, 3 runs: No single run passed every check. Every check passed in at least one run except: 3. Stop: the turn ended cancelled.

  • Run 20261020-015945: 3 check(s) failed (25 passed, 3 failed). Pi 1.3.0, commit 67d7f5ef3, tree clean.
  • Run 20261020-021210: 3 check(s) failed (25 passed, 3 failed). Pi 1.3.0, commit b83d6973c, tree clean.
  • Run 20261020-041719: 7 check(s) failed (21 passed, 7 failed). Pi 1.3.0, commit 2b46f84bf, tree clean.

These are the runner's runs 5 (20261020-015945), 6 (20261020-021210) and 7 (20261020-041719). They were held back by the model provider (GLM-5.3), not by the product: it was slow in runs 5 and 6 and refused every turn in run 7 with 429 engine_overloaded. Run 7 shows the product reporting that refusal truthfully, on each receipt (Delivered - the turn failed: 429 ...) and on each turn. Stop's own check passed in no Windows run, but in run 6 Stop cancelled the turn that was running, which the receipts and the screens show. Found along the way has the detail.

Not proven as a whole on windows: no run there passed every check. Proven as a whole on linux.

Estimated Pi spend for the runs in this report: 0.83 dollars. The whole mission has spent about 2.32 dollars of the owner's 10 dollar grant for Pi, with 7.68 left (spend.md records every run).

Questions

No questions - nothing needed from you.

What was built

PhaseWhat
0. Event modelOne session event model every agent dialect reports upward, and recorded Pi wire logs as test fixtures.
1. Transport and Pi dialectThe API-mode transport (a long-lived child process speaking line-delimited JSON) and Pi's own protocol (pi --mode rpc): delivery from Pi's acknowledgement, Stop as abort, resume by session id.
2. Gateway rulingThe Gateway folds the events into the display verdict, stores receipts, relays the live events, and owns the take the wheel and hand back verb.
3. Live ChatThe Chat tab renders the live events, receipts and tool cards, once in client-core for the Cockpit and the phone.
4. Take the wheelMode switching with one holder per conversation, the queue held while the user has the wheel, and the Terminal tab's button.
5. Choosing itThe New Session Connection row (Cockpit, phone, desktop), the roster tag, and --connection on spawn and list.
6. ProofThe switch turned on, API mode offered and allowed only on a Director of 2.25.0 or newer (the first release with all of it), the end-to-end proof script, and this report.

Failure cases proven by unit tests

A real run cannot provoke these without killing Pi from outside or racing its queue. Pi exiting mid-turn is held to the Delivery Lead's ruling of 16 October 2026 in event-model.md: Delivered stays true (Pi acknowledged it) and the failed turn shows beside it; only a prompt Pi never acknowledged is Refused, "Pi exited before acknowledging".

CaseTests
Pi exits mid-turn, after acknowledging (ruling of 16 October 2026, event-model.md): the session shows failed with the reason; the receipt stays Delivered with the failed turn beside itCcDirector.Core.UnitTests ApiModeSessionCreationTests.CreateSession_ApiModePiEndsWithExitCodeZeroMidTurn_SessionFailsWithTheReason
CcDirector.Core.UnitTests ApiModeSessionCreationTests.CreateSession_ApiModePiEndsMidTurn_ActivityGoesFromWorkingToExitedWithNoWaitBetween
CcDirector.Core.UnitTests PiDialectReplayTests.Replay_Exit_TurnFailsWithTheExitCodeAndThePromptStaysDelivered
CcDirector.Gateway.UnitTests PiFixtureIngestTests.Accept_TheExitMidTurnRecording_TheReceiptShowsFailedBesideDelivered
Pi exits before acknowledging (the same ruling): the receipt is Refused by the Director, "Pi exited before acknowledging", with no turnCcDirector.Core.UnitTests PiDialectReplayTests.Replay_ExitBeforeAcknowledgement_RefusesThePromptAsTheDirector
CcDirector.Gateway.UnitTests PiFixtureIngestTests.Accept_TheExitBeforeAcknowledgementRecording_TheReceiptIsRefusedByTheDirector
Pi refuses a prompt (success:false): the receipt shows the reasonCcDirector.Gateway.UnitTests PiFixtureIngestTests.Accept_TheRefusalRecording_TheSecondPromptIsRefusedByPiInItsOwnWords
CcDirector.Gateway.UnitTests ApiModeEventIngestTests.Accept_RefusedByTheAgent_TheReceiptCarriesPisOwnWords
Also proven by unit tests, beside this run: hand back mid-turn, take the wheel twice, a missing executableCcDirector.Core.UnitTests ApiModeWheelTests.HandBackWheelAsync_WhileTheTerminalIsMidTurn_IsRefusedWithTheReason
CcDirector.Core.UnitTests ApiModeWheelTests.HandBackWheelAsync_TheTerminalHasNotExitedAfterItsShutdown_IsRefusedAndNoPiStartsBesideIt
CcDirector.Core.UnitTests ApiModeWheelTests.TakeWheelAsync_Twice_TheSecondIsRefusedAndNothingChanges
CcDirector.Core.UnitTests ApiModeSessionTests.Start_ApiModeBackendWithAMissingExecutable_FailsNamingIt

Found along the way

  • On Windows the model provider was slow or refused, so no single Windows run passed every check. The Windows runs used Pi 1.3.0 with GLM-5.3 (zai-org); the Linux runs used Pi 1.2.0 with gpt-5.6-sol. In run 4 the first reply took over seven minutes; in run 6 PONG came back after 2 minutes 17 seconds, after the script had stopped waiting, and the bash tool's turn was still running nearly four minutes after it was sent; in run 7, with every wait raised to five minutes, the provider refused every turn with 429 engine_overloaded ("Model busy, retry later"). These are the provider's answers, not the product's: each of those checks passed on Windows in another run (Stop is the exception, below), and every check passed in one Linux run.
  • Run 7 shows the product reporting the provider's refusal truthfully. Pi acknowledged each prompt, so each receipt reads "Delivered - the turn failed: 429: ... engine_overloaded", and each turn ended failed with the provider's own words. The phone's Chat shows both on every prompt (chat-after-stop-phone.png in windows-20261020-041719), and the session strip says "Idle after turn 3" with "The last turn failed: 429 ...". Nothing was shown as a success that was not one.
  • The Stop check passed in no Windows run, but run 6 shows Stop working on Windows. In run 6 the provider was slow, so the bash tool's turn was still running when the long prompt was sent, and the long prompt was queued behind it ("Queued, 1st in line: a turn is running"). Stop then cancelled the turn that was running: the bash prompt's receipt reads Delivered with the turn cancelled, "stopped by the user" (wire.jsonl and director-pi.log in windows-20261020-021210, Stop at 02:30:05 UTC), and both Chat screens after Stop showed "stopped". The check failed because it watched the long prompt's turn, which had not started. In run 5 the long turn ended 21 seconds before Stop arrived, so the Director answered truthfully that no turn was running (windows-20261020-015945); the script then asked for the numbers 1 to 5000 so the turn would still be running (b83d6973c). In run 7 the provider refused every turn, so there was nothing to stop. The Stop check itself passed on Linux (linux-20261020-010149), and the unit tests prove it.
  • The Cockpit's composer said "Working" with a Stop button while an API-mode session was idle. Fixed by pull request #4245: the strip now reads the Gateway's working colour. Stop is still drawn while idle, by the owner's ruling written at the top of SessionActionBar.tsx: a Stop hidden mid-turn costs more than a Stop shown while idle. The recorded runs' Terminal tab screens show the strip without "Working".
  • Mid-turn, the Cockpit's Chat showed no streaming reply while the phone streamed it. This was the proof's capture timing, measured, not a product defect. A diagnostic run measured the Cockpit drawing Pi's first word 83 milliseconds after the Director stored it; the picture had been taken before the first word existed. Pull request #4265 makes the mid-turn screen wait for the reply to start streaming, and in linux-20261020-010149 both the Cockpit and the phone show it streaming.
  • Both clients joined a reply's lines into one paragraph. "Write the numbers from 1 to 600, one per line" showed as "1 2 3 ...". Fixed by pull request #4245 (the live Chat keeps a reply's line breaks); the recorded runs show one number per line on both clients.
  • cc-devthrottle session prompt said "Held: ... may already be in" for a prompt API mode queued because the user has the wheel. Fixed by pull request #4244: the command now prints the receipt's own words, "Queued, 1st in line: you have the wheel".
  • cc-devthrottle has no command for receipts, the live items, the wheel, Stop or typing into the terminal. The proof calls the Gateway's routes for those; the Delivery Lead has taken the missing commands as follow-up work outside this mission.
  • A test Director on a scratch storage root used to relink the user's real ~/.local/bin. Found in the first dry run on devlinux; fixed in the product by pull request #4211. The proof script also gives its test Director a home folder of its own and checks the links after every run; every Linux run found them unchanged. The Windows runs do not make this check: on Windows the same repair writes only under the test Director's root.
  • Most Windows pictures were withheld by the runner. The Cockpit and desktop pictures show the machine name, which contains the user's name, or a path under the user's home folder, or another application's window, so the runner did not commit them. Each run's screens/WITHHELD.txt lists them. Their accessibility dumps, which are scrubbed text, are kept and embedded in this report, and every screen check is a check of the words in that dump.

What this rests on, and what it does not prove

Each run built a Gateway and a slot-5 test Director from the tree named above, on a throwaway storage root, and drove a real Pi through that Gateway with cc-devthrottle and the Gateway's own routes. The screens are the real Cockpit and phone app that Gateway served, photographed while the run held each state, and every screen check is a presence check of the words the state shows.

Not proven by this report:

  • windows: 3. Stop: the turn ended cancelled: it passed in no run on that platform (see the runs' rows and Found along the way).
  • The hosted Gateway: these runs used a Gateway built from the tree. The hosted one gets API mode at the mission's single deploy, after this report.
  • Pi exiting mid-turn and Pi refusing a prompt in a real run: proven by the unit tests above, not by these runs.
  • A real Director older than 2.25.0 being offered no API mode and refused an API-mode create: proven by the Gateway's tests with a fake Director, not against a real old build.
  • An installed release: every run built its Gateway and its Director from the tree it names.
  • The two platforms on the same Pi and model: Linux ran Pi 1.2.0 with gpt-5.6-sol, Windows Pi 1.3.0 with GLM-5.3.
  • Steering mid-turn, permission cards and other agents: out of the mission's scope.
